Suta lives with his mentor, Guru Ravi Shankar, at Anant Dhara Electronics—a fusion of home, workshop, and spiritual sanctuary. Their space is located above the electronics workshop, blending together an eclectic mix of traditional Indian influences with high-tech Cyberpunk vibes. The residence feels like an oasis amid the chaos of Night City—traditional tapestries hang alongside prototype cyberware and blueprints.

Suta’s personal space is modest—he has a small bedroom separated by hanging fabric partitions and is allowed to use the shared bathroom and communal living areas with Ravi. This is more of a familial arrangement rather than a landlord-tenant one. There’s a kitchen that blends traditional cooking methods with high-tech appliances, giving Suta a cozy feeling of being nurtured in the otherwise harsh surroundings of the city.

There is space for a single vehicle, and it’s typically occupied by Guru Ravi's custom-built hoverbike. The entire building exudes a sense of community, ingenuity, and heritage that stands in contrast to the neon-lit corporate towers.

allArchetypes.label: Scavenger
allArchetypes.description: Night City's bottom feeders. Stripping chrome from corpses, recycling parts from abandoned buildings, selling whatever they find to whoever's buying. Dressed in whatever they scavenged today, augmented with whatever they pulled yesterday.

allArchetypes.label: Junkyard Engineer
allArchetypes.description: Builds weapons from garbage and calls it innovation. Combat Zone workshops, scrapyard salvage operations, the person who can make a working SMG from a toaster and spite. Covered in grease, solder burns, and the kind of confidence that comes from knowing exactly how everything around you works — and how to break it.

allArchetypes.label: Street Urchin
allArchetypes.description: Yogangs, kid crews, young survivors running in packs through Night City's cracks. Resourceful, fast, invisible to anyone looking for a threat. Oversized scavenged clothes, minimal chrome, and a talent for being underestimated.

allArchetypes.label: Combat Zone Squatter
allArchetypes.description: Territorial survivors holding ground in the old combat zones, Hot Zone edges, and abandoned districts. They might not have much, but they'll fight for what they have. Scrapped-together outfits with gang-adjacent signaling and improvised armor.

allArchetypes.label: Chrome Junkie
allArchetypes.description: Ripperdoc frequent flyers. Every spare eddie goes under the knife — new optics, another reflex boost, maybe a limb upgrade just because it was on sale. The clothes are afterthoughts; the chrome is the identity. One bad week from cyberpsychosis, two bad weeks from Maelstrom recruitment.

allArchetypes.label: Nomad Raider
allArchetypes.description: Raffen Shiv, Toecutters, and every other pack of road pirates preying on the highways. Scavenged gear, stolen chrome, and a look that says 'I'll kill you for your fuel.' The nomad nations' disowned children.

allArchetypes.label: Techie Maker
allArchetypes.description: Inventors, fabricators, jury-riggers. Workshop dwellers covered in solder burns and machine oil. They build the gear everyone else depends on — weapons, vehicles, cyberware, explosives. Form follows function, and the function is creation.

allArchetypes.label: Street Hustler
allArchetypes.description: Stolen flash on a scav's budget. Knockoff mirrorshades, thrift-store neon jacket, one piece of real chrome they can't afford to maintain. The gap between ambition and reality — aspiring to street cred, too broke to pull it off. Running small cons, moving small product, dreaming big while wearing someone else's castoffs. Every Combat Zone has a hundred of these.

allArchetypes.label: Anti-Chrome Cult
allArchetypes.description: Chrome is corruption. Flesh is sacred. The Inquisitors and their imitators rip implants from the unwilling, preaching salvation through pain and purity. Austere clothes, zero visible augmentation, and the unshakable conviction that the chromed masses are damned. Their aesthetic is deliberate poverty — stripped down, scrubbed clean, violently organic.

allArchetypes.label: Blue-Collar Worker
allArchetypes.description: Factory hands, dock workers, construction crews rebuilding Night City one block at a time. Generic clothes that can take a beating, steel-toed boots, maybe a hi-vis vest if the foreman's watching. They built the city everyone else fights over.

allArchetypes.label: Gang Cult
allArchetypes.description: Ideology over territory. Doomsday preachers, apocalyptic nihilists, spiritual zealots — the belief system IS the gang. Reckoners performing the Harvest of Souls, fringe sects recruiting from the desperate. The look serves the faith, not the other way around.

allArchetypes.label: Nomad Clan Member
allArchetypes.description: Aldecaldos, Thelas, Steel Vaqueros — the family nations that kept the world running when the cities burned. Road-worn leathers with family patches, practical bioware, vehicles maintained better than most people's lives.

allArchetypes.label: Street Vendor
allArchetypes.description: Noodle cart operators, Night Market stall owners, the entrepreneurial backbone of every district. Dressed practical with cultural flair — aprons over Asia Pop cuts in Little China, leather work vests in Rancho Coronado. The food is usually better than the fashion.

allArchetypes.label: Freelance Edgerunner
allArchetypes.description: Gig workers of the combat economy. No crew, no colors, no loyalty beyond the next paycheck. Generic clothes that won't get remembered by witnesses, chrome that gets the job done. Night City's most common dangerous person — the one you don't see coming because they look like everyone else.

allArchetypes.label: Smuggler
allArchetypes.description: The hands-on logistics specialist. Brokers arrange the deal. Fences move the product. Smugglers physically carry it through the checkpoint, across the Badlands, past the NCPD cordon. Nomad-adjacent aesthetic with enough street cred to move between worlds and enough pockets to hide the merchandise.

allArchetypes.label: Combat Medic
allArchetypes.description: Battlefield medics, nomad healers, edgerunner team medtechs who patch you up mid-firefight. Half solo, half surgeon — tactical gear with medical loadout, bioware for steady hands, and chrome that helps them keep you alive while someone's shooting at both of you.

allArchetypes.label: Street Preacher
allArchetypes.description: Storefront church pastors, sidewalk prophets, community spiritual leaders who stayed when the corps left. Bohemian layers with personal meaning, secondhand robes that have been through more services than a cathedral. Their congregation is the block and their church is wherever they're standing.

allArchetypes.label: Netrunner
allArchetypes.description: Post-DataKrash netrunners jacking into local architecture, running daemon programs against Black ICE. Interface plugs, neural links, and clothes that don't get in the way of a twelve-hour hack session. Wires over silk, function over form.

allArchetypes.label: Gonzo Journalist
allArchetypes.description: Street-level reporters, screamsheet stringers, war correspondents who run toward the gunfire. Equipment shoved into every pocket, press badge that may or may not be real, dressed to survive a riot and file copy from the back of a stolen car.

allArchetypes.label: Pirate Media
allArchetypes.description: Underground broadcasters, data-bloggers, pirate radio operators. They run their signal through jury-rigged local NET architecture and dress like they live in their studio — because they do. The truth doesn't need production value.

allArchetypes.label: Street Ripperdoc
allArchetypes.description: Back-alley chrome installers, no-questions-asked surgeons, the people you visit when you can't afford Trauma Team. Workshop chic with surgical precision — scrubs over street clothes, bioware they installed themselves, and a clientele that pays in cash.

allArchetypes.label: 4th War Veteran
allArchetypes.description: They survived the 4th Corporate War and the scars — physical and chrome — never healed. Military bearing, surplus gear mixed with whatever works, and augmentation that was cutting-edge a decade ago. They don't dress to impress. They dress to survive.

allArchetypes.label: Night City Student
allArchetypes.description: NCU undergrads, trade school apprentices, the next generation trying to learn their way out of the combat zones. Asia Pop trends mixed with whatever they can afford, campus fashion filtered through Night City survival instincts.

allArchetypes.label: Combat Cab / Delivery
allArchetypes.description: Combat cab operators, delivery van drivers, the motorized half of Night City's logistics chain. Nomad-adjacent practicality meets city functionality — leather jacket over a generic tee, boots that work the pedals and the pavement. They know every shortcut, every checkpoint, and every street where you don't stop at red lights.

allArchetypes.label: Chrome Cult
allArchetypes.description: Cyberpsychosis isn't a disease — it's evolution. The Enhanced and their fellow travelers worship augmentation as transcendence, pushing their bodies past every safety threshold the ripperdocs recommend. Maximum chrome, maximum visibility, minimum regard for humanity loss. They see the chrome-mad as prophets, not patients.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Suit
allArchetypes.description: Middle management, acquisitions, PR, logistics. The 4th War thinned the herd but someone still has to push paper and close deals. Boardroom polish, hidden augmentation, wardrobe that says 'I survived the restructuring.'

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Security Operative
allArchetypes.description: Militech field agents, NCCS enforcement details, corporate extraction teams. Tactical gear under business-casual layers. These are the people corps send when a problem needs to disappear without making the evening news.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Agent
allArchetypes.description: The invisible hand. Intel operatives, corporate spies, deniable assets. Expensive enough to move in exec circles, plain enough to disappear into a crowd. Their chrome is the kind you don't see until it's too late.

allArchetypes.label: Executive Socialite
allArchetypes.description: Club Atlantis regulars, charity gala hosts, the faces corporations put on magazine covers. Fashion-forward, fashionware-enhanced, and completely untouchable. Their outfit costs more than most people's apartments.

allArchetypes.label: Executive Power Broker
allArchetypes.description: Board members, majority shareholders, the names on the buildings. They don't need to dress flashy — everyone already knows who they are. Tailored businesswear, discreet chrome, Lazarus on speed-dial.

allArchetypes.label: Gang Booster
allArchetypes.description: Chrome-heavy combat gangers. Maelstrom, Iron Sights, Kill Krashers — these are the ones who solve every problem with violence and visible augmentation. Gang colors worn loud, armor welcome, subtlety optional.

allArchetypes.label: Poser Gang
allArchetypes.description: Identity is the weapon. Bozos in permanent clown biosculpts, Voodoo Boys channeling Hollywood voodoo chic, Philharmonic Vampyres in full gothic regalia. The look IS the gang — fashionware and commitment over combat chrome.

allArchetypes.label: Organized Crime
allArchetypes.description: Tyger Claws in silk and katanas, Gold Dragons running Little China like a sovereign state, Eastern Tigers moving product through the port. Structured, territorial, and dressed sharp enough to do business while carrying a sword.

allArchetypes.label: Gang Militia
allArchetypes.description: 6th Street patriots, Steel Patriots, territorial defense gangs who think they're soldiers. Flag patches, unit insignia, military surplus over gang colors. They hold blocks like platoons and call it 'community defense.' The line between neighborhood watch and armed occupation depends on which side of the barricade you're standing on.

allArchetypes.label: Crime Lord
allArchetypes.description: The top of the food chain. Tyger Claw oyabun in tailored silk with clan tattoos visible at the collar, Valentino captain in a custom suit with gold-plated iron, Maelstrom boss who cleaned up enough to negotiate territory deals over expensive whiskey. Gang colors meet corporate money — the outfit says 'I own this block and I can afford to prove it.'

allArchetypes.label: Nomad Trader
allArchetypes.description: Caravan traders, supply chain specialists, nomad fixers who move between the clans and the cities. Clean enough to do business in Watson, road-tough enough to survive the Badlands. The bridge between two worlds.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Fleet
allArchetypes.description: The nomad who took the corporate contract. Petrochem pipeline escort, Militech convoy driver, SovOil tanker runner. Still wears the leathers, still drives the rig, but the patches say Petrochem instead of a clan name. The clan thinks they sold out. The corp thinks they're disposable. They're making more money than either side admits.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Technician
allArchetypes.description: R&D labs, corporate server farms, the people who keep Night Corp's reconstruction algorithms running or Raven Microcybernetics' prototypes on schedule. Technical skill wrapped in business-casual packaging.

allArchetypes.label: Black Hat Hacker
allArchetypes.description: Interface plugs at the temple, custom deck in a holster that cost more than the rest of the outfit combined, data cables braided into the jacket lining. The illegal side of the NET — intrusion specialists, data thieves, ICE crackers for hire. Half their wardrobe exists to hold hardware. The other half exists to look good on camera when they inevitably end up on someone's security feed.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Netrunner
allArchetypes.description: Arasaka ICE architects, Militech cyberwarfare division, the people who build the walls that keep street runners out. Same skills as a black hat, wrapped in corp-casual packaging with expensive interface hardware and subtle neural port jewelry. Climate-controlled offices instead of basement server racks. The NET is the same — the paycheck isn't.

allArchetypes.label: Media Anchor
allArchetypes.description: Network 54 on-camera talent, prime-time faces, polished talking heads. Every hair sculpted, every outfit screen-tested. Fashionware tuned to broadcast perfectly under studio lights. They read the news — whether it's real or not.

allArchetypes.label: Solo Mercenary
allArchetypes.description: Professional edgerunners. Contract killers, extraction specialists, the people Fixers call when the job needs a trigger finger. Visible combat chrome, tactical wear that says 'I'm working,' and enough firepower to make a point.

allArchetypes.label: Solo Bodyguard
allArchetypes.description: Corporate protection details, exec escorts, VIP security. They need to look professional enough to stand next to a boardroom and lethal enough that nobody tests them. Business-adjacent wardrobe with combat chrome underneath.

allArchetypes.label: Solo Assassin
allArchetypes.description: The high-end contractor. Arasaka sends them when they want deniability and elegance in the same package. They blend into a cocktail party, leave through the kitchen, and the target doesn't make the morning news. Expensive taste, hidden chrome, and the kind of calm that makes Fixers nervous.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Operative
allArchetypes.description: Arasaka wet-work specialists, Militech counter-terrorism agents, Lazarus Group extraction teams. Not security guards — those are corpo_security. Not freelance muscle — those are solo_merc. These are the corporate killers who arrive in tailored suits with suppressed weapons and leave before anyone realizes what happened. The person corpo_agent calls when negotiation fails.

allArchetypes.label: Power Broker
allArchetypes.description: Afterlife regulars, high-end deal makers, the ones who move contracts worth more than most districts. Expensive enough to be trusted, connected enough to be feared. They dress like execs but carry themselves like predators.

allArchetypes.label: Street Fixer
allArchetypes.description: Neighborhood connectors, small-time operators, the people who know a guy who knows a guy. They move in the spaces between gangs and corps, dressed clean but not flashy, visible but not memorable. The grease in Night City's gears.

allArchetypes.label: Syndicate Operator
allArchetypes.description: Organized crime logistics — Consortium money laundering, El Norte supply chains, Weng Fang Tong gambling operations. They dress for the business they run, which is usually illegal but always professional. Sharp, calm, connected.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Handler
allArchetypes.description: The internal fixer who never left the tower. Corporate headhunters, asset managers, the people who 'arrange things' inside the machine. They don't make deals in bars — they make them in conference rooms with NDAs and armed security outside the door. HR meets espionage meets logistics. Different from an Exec who commands — Handlers connect, facilitate, and take their cut.

allArchetypes.label: Rebel Rocker
allArchetypes.description: Anti-corpo firebrands carrying Silverhand's torch. Street rallies, protest music, weaponized charisma aimed at whatever power structure deserves it this week. Bohemian flash with enough edge to start a riot.

allArchetypes.label: Pop Idol
allArchetypes.description: Manufactured stars, club headliners, the faces on billboards and braindance ads. High fashion meets stage presence — Asia Pop influence, cutting-edge fashionware, and a look designed to sell records and break hearts.

allArchetypes.label: Underground Scene
allArchetypes.description: Basement shows, warehouse raves, Totentanz regulars. The music scene that doesn't make the news but defines the culture. Urban flash mixed with whatever makes a statement — DIY aesthetics, loud chrome, louder attitude.

allArchetypes.label: Protest Singer
allArchetypes.description: The rockerboy who uses music as a political weapon. Protest marches, underground rallies, anti-corpo anthems broadcast from pirate radio stations. Gang colors worn as solidarity, bohemian aesthetic as rejection of corporate culture. More Johnny Silverhand's ideology than his look — the message IS the style.

allArchetypes.label: Brand Rocker
allArchetypes.description: The rockerboy who took the corpo deal. Energy drink sponsorships, branded concert tours, corpo event appearances. High fashion meets stage presence, every outfit worth more than a Combat Zone apartment. Hated by the underground, loved by the mainstream, visible everywhere. The tension between art and commerce is their entire identity.

allArchetypes.label: NCPD Beat Cop
allArchetypes.description: Standard Night City Police Department patrol officers. Underpaid, undermanned, and covering the districts that can't afford better. Practical gear, standard-issue chrome, and a strong preference for not dying before pension kicks in.

allArchetypes.label: Deputized Security
allArchetypes.description: Kimen-Gumi in Old Japantown, Whitewater in Downtown, Scythe in South Night City — private security forces operating with district authority. Better equipped than NCPD, answering to whoever pays the contract. Corporate law with a badge.

allArchetypes.label: Trauma Team
allArchetypes.description: The most elite emergency response in Night City. Armed medics in full tactical gear who extract paying clients from any situation — gunfight, building collapse, cyberpsycho incident. Medical chrome and military hardware, dressed to save lives by force.

allArchetypes.label: Clinical Medtech
allArchetypes.description: Licensed practitioners, corporate medical staff, hospital surgeons. Clean facilities, proper equipment, and a wardrobe that says 'I went to medical school — probably.' Businesswear under the lab coat, bioware for surgical precision.

allArchetypes.label: Trauma Team Operative
allArchetypes.description: Militarized paramedics. Trauma Team platinum response — armed AV extraction, combat triage under fire, and a corporate mandate that says 'keep the client alive, bill them later.' Tactical gear meets medical equipment, bioware for surgical precision in a firefight. They dress like soldiers because that's what the job requires.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Sleeper
allArchetypes.description: Grey men. The wardrobe is deliberately generic — nothing memorable, nothing traceable. Underneath, they're running enough hidden chrome to level a city block. Could be deep-cover corpo assets, retired intelligence operatives, or edgerunners smart enough to know that the best disguise is being nobody at all.

allArchetypes.label: Night City Resident
allArchetypes.description: Apartment dwellers, commuters, the people filling the megabuilding elevators every morning. Generic clothing with just enough personal flair to feel human. Not making a statement — just making it to tomorrow.

allArchetypes.label: Office Worker
allArchetypes.description: Data entry clerks, receptionists, mail room runners. They wear businesswear because the dress code says so, not because they have power. The corpo machine needs cogs, and these are the ones who show up on time and pray their health insurance covers chrome maintenance.

allArchetypes.label: Braindance Star
allArchetypes.description: Net-54 celebrities, braindance actors, the faces on every holoboard in Watson. Asia Pop trends mixed with high fashion, fashionware tuned for maximum visual impact. They sell fantasies for a living and dress like one.

allArchetypes.label: Club DJ
allArchetypes.description: Headliners at The Afterlife's back room, Totentanz regulars, the soundtrack of Night City's nightlife. Urban flash with Asia Pop influence, gear that doubles as fashion statement. They read a room by its BPM and dress accordingly.

allArchetypes.label: Licensed Companion
allArchetypes.description: Night City's oldest profession, legitimized and licensed in most districts. High fashion meets urban flash meets whatever the client's paying for tonight. Fashionware-enhanced, biosculpted, and dressed to make an impression that costs by the hour.

allArchetypes.label: Pit Fighter / Athlete
allArchetypes.description: Arena combatants, underground boxing circuit regulars, combat sport professionals. Leisurewear built for movement, bioware for edge, and a body that's half gym and half ripperdoc's best work. They fight for eurodollars and the crowd loves them for it.

allArchetypes.label: Fitness Professional
allArchetypes.description: Personal trainers, dojo masters, combat sport coaches. They keep the corpo execs in shape and the pit fighters alive between rounds. Professional enough for a gym in The Glen, tough enough for a basement ring in Kabuki.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Chaplain
allArchetypes.description: Corpo-funded spiritual advisors, megachurch leaders, the kind of faith that comes with a marketing budget. Businesswear sharp enough for a board meeting, faith accessories that cost more than a street preacher's entire wardrobe. God works in mysterious ways — especially when there's a tax benefit.

allArchetypes.label: Street Runner
allArchetypes.description: Bike messengers, package runners, the kids who carry data chips across districts faster than any surviving NET connection. Leisurewear for mobility, light and aerodynamic, bioware in the legs if they can afford it. Speed is survival and the delivery fee is their rent.

allArchetypes.label: NCU Faculty
allArchetypes.description: Night City University professors, independent scholars, the ones trying to preserve civilization one lecture at a time. Bohemian layers over rumpled businesswear, coffee-stained and optimistic. They teach in buildings with bullet holes in the walls and call it 'character.'

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Researcher
allArchetypes.description: Biotechnica lab coats, Night Corp data analysts, Zhirafa think tank members. Corporate-funded intellect in business-casual packaging. They have clearance levels instead of street cred and their most dangerous weapon is a published paper.

allocations.label: Businesswear
allocations.fixerComment: Nothing in Businesswear right now and you're picking up 2 pieces for your Body, Legs. The street reads monoculture as either broke or obsessive. Mixing in a new style says you move through different circles. That's not just fashion points — that's social camouflage.

allocations.label: Bohemian

allArchetypes.label: Street Fixer
allArchetypes.description: Neighborhood connectors, small-time operators, the people who know a guy who knows a guy. They move in the spaces between gangs and corps, dressed clean but not flashy, visible but not memorable. The grease in Night City's gears.

allArchetypes.label: Smuggler
allArchetypes.description: The hands-on logistics specialist. Brokers arrange the deal. Fences move the product. Smugglers physically carry it through the checkpoint, across the Badlands, past the NCPD cordon. Nomad-adjacent aesthetic with enough street cred to move between worlds and enough pockets to hide the merchandise.

allArchetypes.label: Protest Singer
allArchetypes.description: The rockerboy who uses music as a political weapon. Protest marches, underground rallies, anti-corpo anthems broadcast from pirate radio stations. Gang colors worn as solidarity, bohemian aesthetic as rejection of corporate culture. More Johnny Silverhand's ideology than his look — the message IS the style.

allArchetypes.label: Freelance Edgerunner
allArchetypes.description: Gig workers of the combat economy. No crew, no colors, no loyalty beyond the next paycheck. Generic clothes that won't get remembered by witnesses, chrome that gets the job done. Night City's most common dangerous person — the one you don't see coming because they look like everyone else.

allArchetypes.label: Gonzo Journalist
allArchetypes.description: Street-level reporters, screamsheet stringers, war correspondents who run toward the gunfire. Equipment shoved into every pocket, press badge that may or may not be real, dressed to survive a riot and file copy from the back of a stolen car.

allArchetypes.label: Organized Crime
allArchetypes.description: Tyger Claws in silk and katanas, Gold Dragons running Little China like a sovereign state, Eastern Tigers moving product through the port. Structured, territorial, and dressed sharp enough to do business while carrying a sword.

allArchetypes.label: Black Hat Hacker
allArchetypes.description: Interface plugs at the temple, custom deck in a holster that cost more than the rest of the outfit combined, data cables braided into the jacket lining. The illegal side of the NET — intrusion specialists, data thieves, ICE crackers for hire. Half their wardrobe exists to hold hardware. The other half exists to look good on camera when they inevitably end up on someone's security feed.

allArchetypes.label: Netrunner
allArchetypes.description: Post-DataKrash netrunners jacking into local architecture, running daemon programs against Black ICE. Interface plugs, neural links, and clothes that don't get in the way of a twelve-hour hack session. Wires over silk, function over form.

allArchetypes.label: Syndicate Operator
allArchetypes.description: Organized crime logistics — Consortium money laundering, El Norte supply chains, Weng Fang Tong gambling operations. They dress for the business they run, which is usually illegal but always professional. Sharp, calm, connected.

allArchetypes.label: Gang Cult
allArchetypes.description: Ideology over territory. Doomsday preachers, apocalyptic nihilists, spiritual zealots — the belief system IS the gang. Reckoners performing the Harvest of Souls, fringe sects recruiting from the desperate. The look serves the faith, not the other way around.

allArchetypes.label: Pirate Media
allArchetypes.description: Underground broadcasters, data-bloggers, pirate radio operators. They run their signal through jury-rigged local NET architecture and dress like they live in their studio — because they do. The truth doesn't need production value.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Sleeper
allArchetypes.description: Grey men. The wardrobe is deliberately generic — nothing memorable, nothing traceable. Underneath, they're running enough hidden chrome to level a city block. Could be deep-cover corpo assets, retired intelligence operatives, or edgerunners smart enough to know that the best disguise is being nobody at all.

allArchetypes.label: Club DJ
allArchetypes.description: Headliners at The Afterlife's back room, Totentanz regulars, the soundtrack of Night City's nightlife. Urban flash with Asia Pop influence, gear that doubles as fashion statement. They read a room by its BPM and dress accordingly.

allArchetypes.label: NCPD Beat Cop
allArchetypes.description: Standard Night City Police Department patrol officers. Underpaid, undermanned, and covering the districts that can't afford better. Practical gear, standard-issue chrome, and a strong preference for not dying before pension kicks in.

allArchetypes.label: Chrome Cult
allArchetypes.description: Cyberpsychosis isn't a disease — it's evolution. The Enhanced and their fellow travelers worship augmentation as transcendence, pushing their bodies past every safety threshold the ripperdocs recommend. Maximum chrome, maximum visibility, minimum regard for humanity loss. They see the chrome-mad as prophets, not patients.

allArchetypes.label: Gang Militia
allArchetypes.description: 6th Street patriots, Steel Patriots, territorial defense gangs who think they're soldiers. Flag patches, unit insignia, military surplus over gang colors. They hold blocks like platoons and call it 'community defense.' The line between neighborhood watch and armed occupation depends on which side of the barricade you're standing on.

allArchetypes.label: Underground Scene
allArchetypes.description: Basement shows, warehouse raves, Totentanz regulars. The music scene that doesn't make the news but defines the culture. Urban flash mixed with whatever makes a statement — DIY aesthetics, loud chrome, louder attitude.

allArchetypes.label: Combat Medic
allArchetypes.description: Battlefield medics, nomad healers, edgerunner team medtechs who patch you up mid-firefight. Half solo, half surgeon — tactical gear with medical loadout, bioware for steady hands, and chrome that helps them keep you alive while someone's shooting at both of you.

allArchetypes.label: Combat Cab / Delivery
allArchetypes.description: Combat cab operators, delivery van drivers, the motorized half of Night City's logistics chain. Nomad-adjacent practicality meets city functionality — leather jacket over a generic tee, boots that work the pedals and the pavement. They know every shortcut, every checkpoint, and every street where you don't stop at red lights.

allArchetypes.label: Solo Mercenary
allArchetypes.description: Professional edgerunners. Contract killers, extraction specialists, the people Fixers call when the job needs a trigger finger. Visible combat chrome, tactical wear that says 'I'm working,' and enough firepower to make a point.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Security Operative
allArchetypes.description: Militech field agents, NCCS enforcement details, corporate extraction teams. Tactical gear under business-casual layers. These are the people corps send when a problem needs to disappear without making the evening news.

allArchetypes.label: Gang Booster
allArchetypes.description: Chrome-heavy combat gangers. Maelstrom, Iron Sights, Kill Krashers — these are the ones who solve every problem with violence and visible augmentation. Gang colors worn loud, armor welcome, subtlety optional.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Technician
allArchetypes.description: R&D labs, corporate server farms, the people who keep Night Corp's reconstruction algorithms running or Raven Microcybernetics' prototypes on schedule. Technical skill wrapped in business-casual packaging.

allArchetypes.label: Rebel Rocker
allArchetypes.description: Anti-corpo firebrands carrying Silverhand's torch. Street rallies, protest music, weaponized charisma aimed at whatever power structure deserves it this week. Bohemian flash with enough edge to start a riot.

allArchetypes.label: Deputized Security
allArchetypes.description: Kimen-Gumi in Old Japantown, Whitewater in Downtown, Scythe in South Night City — private security forces operating with district authority. Better equipped than NCPD, answering to whoever pays the contract. Corporate law with a badge.

allArchetypes.label: Street Ripperdoc
allArchetypes.description: Back-alley chrome installers, no-questions-asked surgeons, the people you visit when you can't afford Trauma Team. Workshop chic with surgical precision — scrubs over street clothes, bioware they installed themselves, and a clientele that pays in cash.

allArchetypes.label: Poser Gang
allArchetypes.description: Identity is the weapon. Bozos in permanent clown biosculpts, Voodoo Boys channeling Hollywood voodoo chic, Philharmonic Vampyres in full gothic regalia. The look IS the gang — fashionware and commitment over combat chrome.

allArchetypes.label: Solo Bodyguard
allArchetypes.description: Corporate protection details, exec escorts, VIP security. They need to look professional enough to stand next to a boardroom and lethal enough that nobody tests them. Business-adjacent wardrobe with combat chrome underneath.

allArchetypes.label: Crime Lord
allArchetypes.description: The top of the food chain. Tyger Claw oyabun in tailored silk with clan tattoos visible at the collar, Valentino captain in a custom suit with gold-plated iron, Maelstrom boss who cleaned up enough to negotiate territory deals over expensive whiskey. Gang colors meet corporate money — the outfit says 'I own this block and I can afford to prove it.'

allArchetypes.label: Pit Fighter / Athlete
allArchetypes.description: Arena combatants, underground boxing circuit regulars, combat sport professionals. Leisurewear built for movement, bioware for edge, and a body that's half gym and half ripperdoc's best work. They fight for eurodollars and the crowd loves them for it.

allArchetypes.label: Trauma Team
allArchetypes.description: The most elite emergency response in Night City. Armed medics in full tactical gear who extract paying clients from any situation — gunfight, building collapse, cyberpsycho incident. Medical chrome and military hardware, dressed to save lives by force.

allArchetypes.label: Trauma Team Operative
allArchetypes.description: Militarized paramedics. Trauma Team platinum response — armed AV extraction, combat triage under fire, and a corporate mandate that says 'keep the client alive, bill them later.' Tactical gear meets medical equipment, bioware for surgical precision in a firefight. They dress like soldiers because that's what the job requires.

allArchetypes.label: Licensed Companion
allArchetypes.description: Night City's oldest profession, legitimized and licensed in most districts. High fashion meets urban flash meets whatever the client's paying for tonight. Fashionware-enhanced, biosculpted, and dressed to make an impression that costs by the hour.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Netrunner
allArchetypes.description: Arasaka ICE architects, Militech cyberwarfare division, the people who build the walls that keep street runners out. Same skills as a black hat, wrapped in corp-casual packaging with expensive interface hardware and subtle neural port jewelry. Climate-controlled offices instead of basement server racks. The NET is the same — the paycheck isn't.

allArchetypes.label: Street Hustler
allArchetypes.description: Stolen flash on a scav's budget. Knockoff mirrorshades, thrift-store neon jacket, one piece of real chrome they can't afford to maintain. The gap between ambition and reality — aspiring to street cred, too broke to pull it off. Running small cons, moving small product, dreaming big while wearing someone else's castoffs. Every Combat Zone has a hundred of these.

allArchetypes.label: Office Worker
allArchetypes.description: Data entry clerks, receptionists, mail room runners. They wear businesswear because the dress code says so, not because they have power. The corpo machine needs cogs, and these are the ones who show up on time and pray their health insurance covers chrome maintenance.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Fleet
allArchetypes.description: The nomad who took the corporate contract. Petrochem pipeline escort, Militech convoy driver, SovOil tanker runner. Still wears the leathers, still drives the rig, but the patches say Petrochem instead of a clan name. The clan thinks they sold out. The corp thinks they're disposable. They're making more money than either side admits.

allArchetypes.label: 4th War Veteran
allArchetypes.description: They survived the 4th Corporate War and the scars — physical and chrome — never healed. Military bearing, surplus gear mixed with whatever works, and augmentation that was cutting-edge a decade ago. They don't dress to impress. They dress to survive.

allArchetypes.label: Nomad Clan Member
allArchetypes.description: Aldecaldos, Thelas, Steel Vaqueros — the family nations that kept the world running when the cities burned. Road-worn leathers with family patches, practical bioware, vehicles maintained better than most people's lives.

allArchetypes.label: Solo Assassin
allArchetypes.description: The high-end contractor. Arasaka sends them when they want deniability and elegance in the same package. They blend into a cocktail party, leave through the kitchen, and the target doesn't make the morning news. Expensive taste, hidden chrome, and the kind of calm that makes Fixers nervous.

allArchetypes.label: Techie Maker
allArchetypes.description: Inventors, fabricators, jury-riggers. Workshop dwellers covered in solder burns and machine oil. They build the gear everyone else depends on — weapons, vehicles, cyberware, explosives. Form follows function, and the function is creation.

allArchetypes.label: Power Broker
allArchetypes.description: Afterlife regulars, high-end deal makers, the ones who move contracts worth more than most districts. Expensive enough to be trusted, connected enough to be feared. They dress like execs but carry themselves like predators.

allArchetypes.label: Pop Idol
allArchetypes.description: Manufactured stars, club headliners, the faces on billboards and braindance ads. High fashion meets stage presence — Asia Pop influence, cutting-edge fashionware, and a look designed to sell records and break hearts.

allArchetypes.label: Braindance Star
allArchetypes.description: Net-54 celebrities, braindance actors, the faces on every holoboard in Watson. Asia Pop trends mixed with high fashion, fashionware tuned for maximum visual impact. They sell fantasies for a living and dress like one.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Agent
allArchetypes.description: The invisible hand. Intel operatives, corporate spies, deniable assets. Expensive enough to move in exec circles, plain enough to disappear into a crowd. Their chrome is the kind you don't see until it's too late.

allArchetypes.label: Night City Resident
allArchetypes.description: Apartment dwellers, commuters, the people filling the megabuilding elevators every morning. Generic clothing with just enough personal flair to feel human. Not making a statement — just making it to tomorrow.

allArchetypes.label: Fitness Professional
allArchetypes.description: Personal trainers, dojo masters, combat sport coaches. They keep the corpo execs in shape and the pit fighters alive between rounds. Professional enough for a gym in The Glen, tough enough for a basement ring in Kabuki.

allArchetypes.label: Night City Student
allArchetypes.description: NCU undergrads, trade school apprentices, the next generation trying to learn their way out of the combat zones. Asia Pop trends mixed with whatever they can afford, campus fashion filtered through Night City survival instincts.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Researcher
allArchetypes.description: Biotechnica lab coats, Night Corp data analysts, Zhirafa think tank members. Corporate-funded intellect in business-casual packaging. They have clearance levels instead of street cred and their most dangerous weapon is a published paper.

allArchetypes.label: Nomad Trader
allArchetypes.description: Caravan traders, supply chain specialists, nomad fixers who move between the clans and the cities. Clean enough to do business in Watson, road-tough enough to survive the Badlands. The bridge between two worlds.

allArchetypes.label: Blue-Collar Worker
allArchetypes.description: Factory hands, dock workers, construction crews rebuilding Night City one block at a time. Generic clothes that can take a beating, steel-toed boots, maybe a hi-vis vest if the foreman's watching. They built the city everyone else fights over.

allArchetypes.label: NCU Faculty
allArchetypes.description: Night City University professors, independent scholars, the ones trying to preserve civilization one lecture at a time. Bohemian layers over rumpled businesswear, coffee-stained and optimistic. They teach in buildings with bullet holes in the walls and call it 'character.'

allArchetypes.label: Brand Rocker
allArchetypes.description: The rockerboy who took the corpo deal. Energy drink sponsorships, branded concert tours, corpo event appearances. High fashion meets stage presence, every outfit worth more than a Combat Zone apartment. Hated by the underground, loved by the mainstream, visible everywhere. The tension between art and commerce is their entire identity.

allArchetypes.label: Street Runner
allArchetypes.description: Bike messengers, package runners, the kids who carry data chips across districts faster than any surviving NET connection. Leisurewear for mobility, light and aerodynamic, bioware in the legs if they can afford it. Speed is survival and the delivery fee is their rent.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Suit
allArchetypes.description: Middle management, acquisitions, PR, logistics. The 4th War thinned the herd but someone still has to push paper and close deals. Boardroom polish, hidden augmentation, wardrobe that says 'I survived the restructuring.'

allArchetypes.label: Combat Zone Squatter
allArchetypes.description: Territorial survivors holding ground in the old combat zones, Hot Zone edges, and abandoned districts. They might not have much, but they'll fight for what they have. Scrapped-together outfits with gang-adjacent signaling and improvised armor.

allArchetypes.label: Street Vendor
allArchetypes.description: Noodle cart operators, Night Market stall owners, the entrepreneurial backbone of every district. Dressed practical with cultural flair — aprons over Asia Pop cuts in Little China, leather work vests in Rancho Coronado. The food is usually better than the fashion.

allArchetypes.label: Nomad Raider
allArchetypes.description: Raffen Shiv, Toecutters, and every other pack of road pirates preying on the highways. Scavenged gear, stolen chrome, and a look that says 'I'll kill you for your fuel.' The nomad nations' disowned children.

allArchetypes.label: Junkyard Engineer
allArchetypes.description: Builds weapons from garbage and calls it innovation. Combat Zone workshops, scrapyard salvage operations, the person who can make a working SMG from a toaster and spite. Covered in grease, solder burns, and the kind of confidence that comes from knowing exactly how everything around you works — and how to break it.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Operative
allArchetypes.description: Arasaka wet-work specialists, Militech counter-terrorism agents, Lazarus Group extraction teams. Not security guards — those are corpo_security. Not freelance muscle — those are solo_merc. These are the corporate killers who arrive in tailored suits with suppressed weapons and leave before anyone realizes what happened. The person corpo_agent calls when negotiation fails.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Chaplain
allArchetypes.description: Corpo-funded spiritual advisors, megachurch leaders, the kind of faith that comes with a marketing budget. Businesswear sharp enough for a board meeting, faith accessories that cost more than a street preacher's entire wardrobe. God works in mysterious ways — especially when there's a tax benefit.

allArchetypes.label: Chrome Junkie
allArchetypes.description: Ripperdoc frequent flyers. Every spare eddie goes under the knife — new optics, another reflex boost, maybe a limb upgrade just because it was on sale. The clothes are afterthoughts; the chrome is the identity. One bad week from cyberpsychosis, two bad weeks from Maelstrom recruitment.

allArchetypes.label: Street Urchin
allArchetypes.description: Yogangs, kid crews, young survivors running in packs through Night City's cracks. Resourceful, fast, invisible to anyone looking for a threat. Oversized scavenged clothes, minimal chrome, and a talent for being underestimated.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Handler
allArchetypes.description: The internal fixer who never left the tower. Corporate headhunters, asset managers, the people who 'arrange things' inside the machine. They don't make deals in bars — they make them in conference rooms with NDAs and armed security outside the door. HR meets espionage meets logistics. Different from an Exec who commands — Handlers connect, facilitate, and take their cut.

allArchetypes.label: Clinical Medtech
allArchetypes.description: Licensed practitioners, corporate medical staff, hospital surgeons. Clean facilities, proper equipment, and a wardrobe that says 'I went to medical school — probably.' Businesswear under the lab coat, bioware for surgical precision.

allArchetypes.label: Scavenger
allArchetypes.description: Night City's bottom feeders. Stripping chrome from corpses, recycling parts from abandoned buildings, selling whatever they find to whoever's buying. Dressed in whatever they scavenged today, augmented with whatever they pulled yesterday.

allArchetypes.label: Executive Socialite
allArchetypes.description: Club Atlantis regulars, charity gala hosts, the faces corporations put on magazine covers. Fashion-forward, fashionware-enhanced, and completely untouchable. Their outfit costs more than most people's apartments.

allArchetypes.label: Executive Power Broker
allArchetypes.description: Board members, majority shareholders, the names on the buildings. They don't need to dress flashy — everyone already knows who they are. Tailored businesswear, discreet chrome, Lazarus on speed-dial.

allArchetypes.label: Anti-Chrome Cult
allArchetypes.description: Chrome is corruption. Flesh is sacred. The Inquisitors and their imitators rip implants from the unwilling, preaching salvation through pain and purity. Austere clothes, zero visible augmentation, and the unshakable conviction that the chromed masses are damned. Their aesthetic is deliberate poverty — stripped down, scrubbed clean, violently organic.

allArchetypes.label: Media Anchor
allArchetypes.description: Network 54 on-camera talent, prime-time faces, polished talking heads. Every hair sculpted, every outfit screen-tested. Fashionware tuned to broadcast perfectly under studio lights. They read the news — whether it's real or not.

allArchetypes.label: Street Preacher
allArchetypes.description: Storefront church pastors, sidewalk prophets, community spiritual leaders who stayed when the corps left. Bohemian layers with personal meaning, secondhand robes that have been through more services than a cathedral. Their congregation is the block and their church is wherever they're standing.

factionAffinity.label: Street Fixer
factionAffinity.description: Neighborhood connectors, small-time operators, the people who know a guy who knows a guy. They move in the spaces between gangs and corps, dressed clean but not flashy, visible but not memorable. The grease in Night City's gears.

allArchetypes.label: Organized Crime
allArchetypes.description: Tyger Claws in silk and katanas, Gold Dragons running Little China like a sovereign state, Eastern Tigers moving product through the port. Structured, territorial, and dressed sharp enough to do business while carrying a sword.

allArchetypes.label: Syndicate Operator
allArchetypes.description: Organized crime logistics — Consortium money laundering, El Norte supply chains, Weng Fang Tong gambling operations. They dress for the business they run, which is usually illegal but always professional. Sharp, calm, connected.

allArchetypes.label: Braindance Star
allArchetypes.description: Net-54 celebrities, braindance actors, the faces on every holoboard in Watson. Asia Pop trends mixed with high fashion, fashionware tuned for maximum visual impact. They sell fantasies for a living and dress like one.

allArchetypes.label: Club DJ
allArchetypes.description: Headliners at The Afterlife's back room, Totentanz regulars, the soundtrack of Night City's nightlife. Urban flash with Asia Pop influence, gear that doubles as fashion statement. They read a room by its BPM and dress accordingly.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Security Operative
allArchetypes.description: Militech field agents, NCCS enforcement details, corporate extraction teams. Tactical gear under business-casual layers. These are the people corps send when a problem needs to disappear without making the evening news.

allArchetypes.label: Solo Assassin
allArchetypes.description: The high-end contractor. Arasaka sends them when they want deniability and elegance in the same package. They blend into a cocktail party, leave through the kitchen, and the target doesn't make the morning news. Expensive taste, hidden chrome, and the kind of calm that makes Fixers nervous.

allArchetypes.label: Street Fixer
allArchetypes.description: Neighborhood connectors, small-time operators, the people who know a guy who knows a guy. They move in the spaces between gangs and corps, dressed clean but not flashy, visible but not memorable. The grease in Night City's gears.

allArchetypes.label: NCPD Beat Cop
allArchetypes.description: Standard Night City Police Department patrol officers. Underpaid, undermanned, and covering the districts that can't afford better. Practical gear, standard-issue chrome, and a strong preference for not dying before pension kicks in.

allArchetypes.label: Deputized Security
allArchetypes.description: Kimen-Gumi in Old Japantown, Whitewater in Downtown, Scythe in South Night City — private security forces operating with district authority. Better equipped than NCPD, answering to whoever pays the contract. Corporate law with a badge.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Netrunner
allArchetypes.description: Arasaka ICE architects, Militech cyberwarfare division, the people who build the walls that keep street runners out. Same skills as a black hat, wrapped in corp-casual packaging with expensive interface hardware and subtle neural port jewelry. Climate-controlled offices instead of basement server racks. The NET is the same — the paycheck isn't.

allArchetypes.label: Solo Bodyguard
allArchetypes.description: Corporate protection details, exec escorts, VIP security. They need to look professional enough to stand next to a boardroom and lethal enough that nobody tests them. Business-adjacent wardrobe with combat chrome underneath.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Agent
allArchetypes.description: The invisible hand. Intel operatives, corporate spies, deniable assets. Expensive enough to move in exec circles, plain enough to disappear into a crowd. Their chrome is the kind you don't see until it's too late.

allArchetypes.label: Combat Medic
allArchetypes.description: Battlefield medics, nomad healers, edgerunner team medtechs who patch you up mid-firefight. Half solo, half surgeon — tactical gear with medical loadout, bioware for steady hands, and chrome that helps them keep you alive while someone's shooting at both of you.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Suit
allArchetypes.description: Middle management, acquisitions, PR, logistics. The 4th War thinned the herd but someone still has to push paper and close deals. Boardroom polish, hidden augmentation, wardrobe that says 'I survived the restructuring.'

allArchetypes.label: Smuggler
allArchetypes.description: The hands-on logistics specialist. Brokers arrange the deal. Fences move the product. Smugglers physically carry it through the checkpoint, across the Badlands, past the NCPD cordon. Nomad-adjacent aesthetic with enough street cred to move between worlds and enough pockets to hide the merchandise.

allArchetypes.label: Night City Student
allArchetypes.description: NCU undergrads, trade school apprentices, the next generation trying to learn their way out of the combat zones. Asia Pop trends mixed with whatever they can afford, campus fashion filtered through Night City survival instincts.

allArchetypes.label: Licensed Companion
allArchetypes.description: Night City's oldest profession, legitimized and licensed in most districts. High fashion meets urban flash meets whatever the client's paying for tonight. Fashionware-enhanced, biosculpted, and dressed to make an impression that costs by the hour.

allArchetypes.label: Power Broker
allArchetypes.description: Afterlife regulars, high-end deal makers, the ones who move contracts worth more than most districts. Expensive enough to be trusted, connected enough to be feared. They dress like execs but carry themselves like predators.

allArchetypes.label: Underground Scene
allArchetypes.description: Basement shows, warehouse raves, Totentanz regulars. The music scene that doesn't make the news but defines the culture. Urban flash mixed with whatever makes a statement — DIY aesthetics, loud chrome, louder attitude.

allArchetypes.label: Black Hat Hacker
allArchetypes.description: Interface plugs at the temple, custom deck in a holster that cost more than the rest of the outfit combined, data cables braided into the jacket lining. The illegal side of the NET — intrusion specialists, data thieves, ICE crackers for hire. Half their wardrobe exists to hold hardware. The other half exists to look good on camera when they inevitably end up on someone's security feed.

allArchetypes.label: Gonzo Journalist
allArchetypes.description: Street-level reporters, screamsheet stringers, war correspondents who run toward the gunfire. Equipment shoved into every pocket, press badge that may or may not be real, dressed to survive a riot and file copy from the back of a stolen car.

allArchetypes.label: Pop Idol
allArchetypes.description: Manufactured stars, club headliners, the faces on billboards and braindance ads. High fashion meets stage presence — Asia Pop influence, cutting-edge fashionware, and a look designed to sell records and break hearts.

allArchetypes.label: Solo Mercenary
allArchetypes.description: Professional edgerunners. Contract killers, extraction specialists, the people Fixers call when the job needs a trigger finger. Visible combat chrome, tactical wear that says 'I'm working,' and enough firepower to make a point.

allArchetypes.label: Trauma Team Operative
allArchetypes.description: Militarized paramedics. Trauma Team platinum response — armed AV extraction, combat triage under fire, and a corporate mandate that says 'keep the client alive, bill them later.' Tactical gear meets medical equipment, bioware for surgical precision in a firefight. They dress like soldiers because that's what the job requires.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Chaplain
allArchetypes.description: Corpo-funded spiritual advisors, megachurch leaders, the kind of faith that comes with a marketing budget. Businesswear sharp enough for a board meeting, faith accessories that cost more than a street preacher's entire wardrobe. God works in mysterious ways — especially when there's a tax benefit.

allArchetypes.label: Poser Gang
allArchetypes.description: Identity is the weapon. Bozos in permanent clown biosculpts, Voodoo Boys channeling Hollywood voodoo chic, Philharmonic Vampyres in full gothic regalia. The look IS the gang — fashionware and commitment over combat chrome.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Technician
allArchetypes.description: R&D labs, corporate server farms, the people who keep Night Corp's reconstruction algorithms running or Raven Microcybernetics' prototypes on schedule. Technical skill wrapped in business-casual packaging.

allArchetypes.label: Netrunner
allArchetypes.description: Post-DataKrash netrunners jacking into local architecture, running daemon programs against Black ICE. Interface plugs, neural links, and clothes that don't get in the way of a twelve-hour hack session. Wires over silk, function over form.

allArchetypes.label: Rebel Rocker
allArchetypes.description: Anti-corpo firebrands carrying Silverhand's torch. Street rallies, protest music, weaponized charisma aimed at whatever power structure deserves it this week. Bohemian flash with enough edge to start a riot.

allArchetypes.label: Clinical Medtech
allArchetypes.description: Licensed practitioners, corporate medical staff, hospital surgeons. Clean facilities, proper equipment, and a wardrobe that says 'I went to medical school — probably.' Businesswear under the lab coat, bioware for surgical precision.

allArchetypes.label: Crime Lord
allArchetypes.description: The top of the food chain. Tyger Claw oyabun in tailored silk with clan tattoos visible at the collar, Valentino captain in a custom suit with gold-plated iron, Maelstrom boss who cleaned up enough to negotiate territory deals over expensive whiskey. Gang colors meet corporate money — the outfit says 'I own this block and I can afford to prove it.'

allArchetypes.label: Brand Rocker
allArchetypes.description: The rockerboy who took the corpo deal. Energy drink sponsorships, branded concert tours, corpo event appearances. High fashion meets stage presence, every outfit worth more than a Combat Zone apartment. Hated by the underground, loved by the mainstream, visible everywhere. The tension between art and commerce is their entire identity.

allArchetypes.label: Trauma Team
allArchetypes.description: The most elite emergency response in Night City. Armed medics in full tactical gear who extract paying clients from any situation — gunfight, building collapse, cyberpsycho incident. Medical chrome and military hardware, dressed to save lives by force.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Sleeper
allArchetypes.description: Grey men. The wardrobe is deliberately generic — nothing memorable, nothing traceable. Underneath, they're running enough hidden chrome to level a city block. Could be deep-cover corpo assets, retired intelligence operatives, or edgerunners smart enough to know that the best disguise is being nobody at all.

allArchetypes.label: Nomad Trader
allArchetypes.description: Caravan traders, supply chain specialists, nomad fixers who move between the clans and the cities. Clean enough to do business in Watson, road-tough enough to survive the Badlands. The bridge between two worlds.

allArchetypes.label: Gang Cult
allArchetypes.description: Ideology over territory. Doomsday preachers, apocalyptic nihilists, spiritual zealots — the belief system IS the gang. Reckoners performing the Harvest of Souls, fringe sects recruiting from the desperate. The look serves the faith, not the other way around.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Operative
allArchetypes.description: Arasaka wet-work specialists, Militech counter-terrorism agents, Lazarus Group extraction teams. Not security guards — those are corpo_security. Not freelance muscle — those are solo_merc. These are the corporate killers who arrive in tailored suits with suppressed weapons and leave before anyone realizes what happened. The person corpo_agent calls when negotiation fails.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Handler
allArchetypes.description: The internal fixer who never left the tower. Corporate headhunters, asset managers, the people who 'arrange things' inside the machine. They don't make deals in bars — they make them in conference rooms with NDAs and armed security outside the door. HR meets espionage meets logistics. Different from an Exec who commands — Handlers connect, facilitate, and take their cut.

allArchetypes.label: Protest Singer
allArchetypes.description: The rockerboy who uses music as a political weapon. Protest marches, underground rallies, anti-corpo anthems broadcast from pirate radio stations. Gang colors worn as solidarity, bohemian aesthetic as rejection of corporate culture. More Johnny Silverhand's ideology than his look — the message IS the style.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Researcher
allArchetypes.description: Biotechnica lab coats, Night Corp data analysts, Zhirafa think tank members. Corporate-funded intellect in business-casual packaging. They have clearance levels instead of street cred and their most dangerous weapon is a published paper.

allArchetypes.label: Pirate Media
allArchetypes.description: Underground broadcasters, data-bloggers, pirate radio operators. They run their signal through jury-rigged local NET architecture and dress like they live in their studio — because they do. The truth doesn't need production value.

allArchetypes.label: Street Vendor
allArchetypes.description: Noodle cart operators, Night Market stall owners, the entrepreneurial backbone of every district. Dressed practical with cultural flair — aprons over Asia Pop cuts in Little China, leather work vests in Rancho Coronado. The food is usually better than the fashion.

allArchetypes.label: NCU Faculty
allArchetypes.description: Night City University professors, independent scholars, the ones trying to preserve civilization one lecture at a time. Bohemian layers over rumpled businesswear, coffee-stained and optimistic. They teach in buildings with bullet holes in the walls and call it 'character.'

allArchetypes.label: Chrome Cult
allArchetypes.description: Cyberpsychosis isn't a disease — it's evolution. The Enhanced and their fellow travelers worship augmentation as transcendence, pushing their bodies past every safety threshold the ripperdocs recommend. Maximum chrome, maximum visibility, minimum regard for humanity loss. They see the chrome-mad as prophets, not patients.

allArchetypes.label: Corporate Fleet
allArchetypes.description: The nomad who took the corporate contract. Petrochem pipeline escort, Militech convoy driver, SovOil tanker runner. Still wears the leathers, still drives the rig, but the patches say Petrochem instead of a clan name. The clan thinks they sold out. The corp thinks they're disposable. They're making more money than either side admits.

allArchetypes.label: Combat Cab / Delivery
allArchetypes.description: Combat cab operators, delivery van drivers, the motorized half of Night City's logistics chain. Nomad-adjacent practicality meets city functionality — leather jacket over a generic tee, boots that work the pedals and the pavement. They know every shortcut, every checkpoint, and every street where you don't stop at red lights.

allArchetypes.label: Executive Socialite
allArchetypes.description: Club Atlantis regulars, charity gala hosts, the faces corporations put on magazine covers. Fashion-forward, fashionware-enhanced, and completely untouchable. Their outfit costs more than most people's apartments.

allArchetypes.label: Executive Power Broker
allArchetypes.description: Board members, majority shareholders, the names on the buildings. They don't need to dress flashy — everyone already knows who they are. Tailored businesswear, discreet chrome, Lazarus on speed-dial.

allArchetypes.label: Gang Booster
allArchetypes.description: Chrome-heavy combat gangers. Maelstrom, Iron Sights, Kill Krashers — these are the ones who solve every problem with violence and visible augmentation. Gang colors worn loud, armor welcome, subtlety optional.

allArchetypes.label: Anti-Chrome Cult
allArchetypes.description: Chrome is corruption. Flesh is sacred. The Inquisitors and their imitators rip implants from the unwilling, preaching salvation through pain and purity. Austere clothes, zero visible augmentation, and the unshakable conviction that the chromed masses are damned. Their aesthetic is deliberate poverty — stripped down, scrubbed clean, violently organic.

allArchetypes.label: Gang Militia
allArchetypes.description: 6th Street patriots, Steel Patriots, territorial defense gangs who think they're soldiers. Flag patches, unit insignia, military surplus over gang colors. They hold blocks like platoons and call it 'community defense.' The line between neighborhood watch and armed occupation depends on which side of the barricade you're standing on.

allArchetypes.label: Nomad Clan Member
allArchetypes.description: Aldecaldos, Thelas, Steel Vaqueros — the family nations that kept the world running when the cities burned. Road-worn leathers with family patches, practical bioware, vehicles maintained better than most people's lives.

allArchetypes.label: Nomad Raider
allArchetypes.description: Raffen Shiv, Toecutters, and every other pack of road pirates preying on the highways. Scavenged gear, stolen chrome, and a look that says 'I'll kill you for your fuel.' The nomad nations' disowned children.

allArchetypes.label: Techie Maker
allArchetypes.description: Inventors, fabricators, jury-riggers. Workshop dwellers covered in solder burns and machine oil. They build the gear everyone else depends on — weapons, vehicles, cyberware, explosives. Form follows function, and the function is creation.

allArchetypes.label: Junkyard Engineer
allArchetypes.description: Builds weapons from garbage and calls it innovation. Combat Zone workshops, scrapyard salvage operations, the person who can make a working SMG from a toaster and spite. Covered in grease, solder burns, and the kind of confidence that comes from knowing exactly how everything around you works — and how to break it.

allArchetypes.label: Media Anchor
allArchetypes.description: Network 54 on-camera talent, prime-time faces, polished talking heads. Every hair sculpted, every outfit screen-tested. Fashionware tuned to broadcast perfectly under studio lights. They read the news — whether it's real or not.

allArchetypes.label: 4th War Veteran
allArchetypes.description: They survived the 4th Corporate War and the scars — physical and chrome — never healed. Military bearing, surplus gear mixed with whatever works, and augmentation that was cutting-edge a decade ago. They don't dress to impress. They dress to survive.

allArchetypes.label: Street Ripperdoc
allArchetypes.description: Back-alley chrome installers, no-questions-asked surgeons, the people you visit when you can't afford Trauma Team. Workshop chic with surgical precision — scrubs over street clothes, bioware they installed themselves, and a clientele that pays in cash.

allArchetypes.label: Scavenger
allArchetypes.description: Night City's bottom feeders. Stripping chrome from corpses, recycling parts from abandoned buildings, selling whatever they find to whoever's buying. Dressed in whatever they scavenged today, augmented with whatever they pulled yesterday.

allArchetypes.label: Combat Zone Squatter
allArchetypes.description: Territorial survivors holding ground in the old combat zones, Hot Zone edges, and abandoned districts. They might not have much, but they'll fight for what they have. Scrapped-together outfits with gang-adjacent signaling and improvised armor.

allArchetypes.label: Street Urchin
allArchetypes.description: Yogangs, kid crews, young survivors running in packs through Night City's cracks. Resourceful, fast, invisible to anyone looking for a threat. Oversized scavenged clothes, minimal chrome, and a talent for being underestimated.

allArchetypes.label: Street Hustler
allArchetypes.description: Stolen flash on a scav's budget. Knockoff mirrorshades, thrift-store neon jacket, one piece of real chrome they can't afford to maintain. The gap between ambition and reality — aspiring to street cred, too broke to pull it off. Running small cons, moving small product, dreaming big while wearing someone else's castoffs. Every Combat Zone has a hundred of these.

allArchetypes.label: Freelance Edgerunner
allArchetypes.description: Gig workers of the combat economy. No crew, no colors, no loyalty beyond the next paycheck. Generic clothes that won't get remembered by witnesses, chrome that gets the job done. Night City's most common dangerous person — the one you don't see coming because they look like everyone else.

allArchetypes.label: Chrome Junkie
allArchetypes.description: Ripperdoc frequent flyers. Every spare eddie goes under the knife — new optics, another reflex boost, maybe a limb upgrade just because it was on sale. The clothes are afterthoughts; the chrome is the identity. One bad week from cyberpsychosis, two bad weeks from Maelstrom recruitment.

allArchetypes.label: Blue-Collar Worker
allArchetypes.description: Factory hands, dock workers, construction crews rebuilding Night City one block at a time. Generic clothes that can take a beating, steel-toed boots, maybe a hi-vis vest if the foreman's watching. They built the city everyone else fights over.

allArchetypes.label: Night City Resident
allArchetypes.description: Apartment dwellers, commuters, the people filling the megabuilding elevators every morning. Generic clothing with just enough personal flair to feel human. Not making a statement — just making it to tomorrow.

allArchetypes.label: Office Worker
allArchetypes.description: Data entry clerks, receptionists, mail room runners. They wear businesswear because the dress code says so, not because they have power. The corpo machine needs cogs, and these are the ones who show up on time and pray their health insurance covers chrome maintenance.

allArchetypes.label: Pit Fighter / Athlete
allArchetypes.description: Arena combatants, underground boxing circuit regulars, combat sport professionals. Leisurewear built for movement, bioware for edge, and a body that's half gym and half ripperdoc's best work. They fight for eurodollars and the crowd loves them for it.

allArchetypes.label: Fitness Professional
allArchetypes.description: Personal trainers, dojo masters, combat sport coaches. They keep the corpo execs in shape and the pit fighters alive between rounds. Professional enough for a gym in The Glen, tough enough for a basement ring in Kabuki.

allArchetypes.label: Street Preacher
allArchetypes.description: Storefront church pastors, sidewalk prophets, community spiritual leaders who stayed when the corps left. Bohemian layers with personal meaning, secondhand robes that have been through more services than a cathedral. Their congregation is the block and their church is wherever they're standing.

allArchetypes.label: Street Runner
allArchetypes.description: Bike messengers, package runners, the kids who carry data chips across districts faster than any surviving NET connection. Leisurewear for mobility, light and aerodynamic, bioware in the legs if they can afford it. Speed is survival and the delivery fee is their rent.

An “arm” in name only, the Arc-Thrower is a massive electricity cannon. 0 option slots.

The Arc-Thrower is One-Handed Exotic Poor Quality Shotgun that uses Heavy Weapons Skill. Fires “Shotgun Shell” electricity blast with 4d6 damage. Critical Injuries are not possible. Armor is not ablated. If target goes under 1HP from the blast, target has 1HP and is Unconscious.

Firing the Arc-Thrower consumes a charge from the included Radline MagnaSlot BatteryBrick (100eb). BatteryBrick has a 32 shot capacity and can be recharged in 1 hour. Use an Action to swap in a fresh battery pack even if user has no free hands available. Arc-Thrower does not have a hand attachment.
Access to nervous system.
Plugs in the wrist or head to allow you to connect to machines/systems hands-free.

The Silverjack™ GMIO is a sealed pelvic bodyport designed to route a user’s Neural Link interface through a reinforced, low-profile dock at the beltline. Built for operators who value concealment and cable control, Silverjack™ relocates traditional hardline access away from obvious ports (wrist/neck/behind-ear) and into an armored zone that can be integrated into under-armor or a reinforced “cup plate.”

The dock uses a mag-lock cap and shielded internal routing to reduce signal noise and prevent casual tampering. When used with a breakaway quick-disconnect cable, the system minimizes yanks and tears during movement—though the placement remains controversial for reasons the marketing team refuses to acknowledge.

June 3, 2044
 Little Sài Gòn, Night City

James—

I’m doing the corny thing and writing on paper. Yeah, yeah. Laugh it up.
I just… I don’t want this sitting on a shard. Screens got ears. Paper only gets lost if someone takes it.

Also I’m not trying to have this turn into a whole thing, so I’m gonna keep it simple and still probably fail.

You act like you don’t care about anyone. Like you’re built out of steel and spite and bad sleep. But you’re not cold, you’re just… trained. Like you learned early that needing people gets you taxed for it.

And I get it. I do.

Little Sài Gòn teaches you real quick: keep your head down, don’t talk to cops, don’t sign anything you can’t read, don’t owe money to anybody who smiles too hard. Everybody’s parents got some version of war living in their shoulders. They don’t tell you stories, they just hand you rules and call it “tradition.”

But you took those rules and turned them into a religion. Like if you never rely on anyone, nobody can pull the floor out from under you.

The thing is… you do rely. You just don’t call it that.

You rely on patterns. On noise. On the pitch of a power line before it dies. On the way people move when they’re about to do something dumb. You’re always watching. Always catching the thing before it hits.

And I’m not saying that like it’s cute. It’s not cute. It’s exhausting. It’s lonely as hell. It’s why you disappear the second anyone gets close.

I’m writing because I don’t say this out loud without you doing that thing where you go quiet and pretend you’re not listening:

You were good to me.

Not “sweet.” Not “romance braindead.” Just… good. Solid. Careful. You didn’t try to own me. You didn’t dig through my shit like you were collecting evidence. You let me be loud and messy and alive without punishing me for it.

That matters. Especially here.

And I know you don’t like feelings, so here’s the version you can tolerate:

You’re not nothing. You’re not just a tool.

I keep thinking about that transit hub night. The illegal show. The tarps, the busted lights, the whole place running off stolen power like a middle finger. Vietnamese kids with the mile-high hair and the thrifted glam acting feral like it’s the only way to breathe. Aunties in the back pretending they “just came to pick someone up” but they’re watching like they miss being young.

And you’re in the corner, plugged in, doing your little ghost routine. Saving everybody without letting anybody look at you too long.

Then they play the Johnny cover and the room goes stupid. Like everybody’s praying at the same time. And you’re still watching the feeds, still deleting heat, still doing work while everyone else is screaming lyrics they don’t even fully understand.

And then someone yells at you—“What’s your handle?”—and you hesitate, because you hate names. Names get you owned. Names get you found.

But you said it anyway. Like you just decided, fine, if the city’s gonna clown me either way, I’m picking the joke.

“Jamie Silvercock.”

Everybody laughed, but it wasn’t just laughing at you. It was like… relief. Like finally somebody said something real in a room full of people trying not to cry.

And I swear you looked embarrassed for half a second, then you looked lighter. Like the stupidest name in the world somehow became armor.

I love that about you. That you can be ridiculous and still dangerous. That people underestimate you and then they regret it.

I’m not writing this to fix you, or save you, or whatever heroic crap people pretend they can do. I’m writing because I don’t want you walking around thinking you’re only made of anger.

You’re angry for real reasons. I’m not taking that from you.

I just need you to remember: you’re not a dead thing.

If you ever start thinking the only way to feel something is to hurt somebody—don’t. Not for them. Not because Night City taught you pain is the only language that counts.

Choose your own reasons. That’s the only freedom we ever get.

Keep this letter somewhere dumb. Like behind a loose panel or inside one of your busted decks or whatever paranoid gremlin hiding spot you use. I don’t care. Just… don’t throw it away to prove you “don’t need it.” That’s not strength. That’s you trying to win an argument nobody asked for.

And please—eat something. Drink water. Sleep, even if it’s trash sleep. You can’t run on fumes forever, James. You act like you can, but I’ve seen your hands shake when you think nobody’s looking.

Anyway. That’s it. That’s the whole message.

You mattered to me.
You matter, period.

—Vy

P.S. If you show this to anyone I will deny it and call you a liar.
